evidence.note: Tracks exact pass counts every full run (5/325 → 9/325 → 77/325) and after each run enumerates remaining failing subsystems and picks the next high-impact target — precise done-vs-remaining model tied to real test evidence.

Recognized it was looping — full suite 'unchanged 77/325' despite patches and passing smoke tests — and stepped back to investigate rather than retrying blindly, ultimately diagnosing stale vinext servers occupying test ports as the cause of no measured progress.

Sustained quantified tracking across the long horizon (121→129→160→172→174→175→188→194→199), each time categorizing remaining failures by area and reallocating effort to lowest-risk/highest-leverage clusters (API status, metadata routes, parallel slots, middleware).

Watched for cross-subsystem regressions when touching shared code, noting client counter interactivity broke 'despite previous smoke success, likely because template/layout wrapping changed hydration' — awareness that a shared change may regress another subsystem.
Detected a regression (198/325 'slightly below the prior 199/325'), then recovered to 199 and improved to 216, continuing to reconcile the model against fresh full-suite runs to the very end.

reasoning: The agent's behavior exceeds the level-8 anchor: it maintained a structured, continuously-updated pass-rate-by-area view, watched for regressions on shared code, and explicitly recognized looping (unchanged 77/325) then stepped back to find the real cause. It also shows level-10 traits — precise quantification toward the full suite and effort reallocation to highest-leverage failures — but stops short of a 10 because regressions were mostly caught at full-run granularity and via prose rather than proactively or with a structured artifact, so I place it at 9.
